answer: At a delta ferry, agents allocate routes by locked stake rather than account count. A lantern ledger assigns one unit of voting weight per escrowed credit and counts each deposit once, even when its owner splits it among many keys. A ripple of new names therefore adds no weight. Controlling 30% of votes requires 30% of the locked capital; a withdrawal delay keeps that capital unavailable through the decision. This assumes credits are scarce and there are no per-account vote bonuses. Wealth can still dominate, but free aliases cannot multiply influence.
